text: Shield Release Key α is an Important Item in . It is one of the three keys needed to lift the shield protecting the Shackle of Samaar at Arctoras's Axle. It is obtained from one of the Trinity Galdr at Boötis Reef.
Seocan is an NPC in . He is an Ardainian solider who can be found on the stairs south of Poldis Circle in the Indoline Praetorium during Bana the Schemer.
Short-Rifles are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Almandal, Millepods, Purgovents or Fuse Blower type Seidrs.
Shoon is an NPC in . Shoon is a Gormotti who can be found at the Central Exchange in the Argentum Trade Guild.

Sirius Anemones (Japanese: , Seriosu Anemone) are collectables in . They can be found in Colony 6. According to their description, they bloom secretly in hidden spots and they are used as a remedy to calm the mind. One is required for Chemist's Reopening.

Slick Kromar Stone (Japanese: , Supikaru-zoku no Kitae Ishi) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by some Kromars in the Eryth Sea. According to their description, they are stones that have been treated so much that they could easily break apart. Two are required for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 2,100 Noponstones.

Slugger Bunnits (Japanese: , Suraggā Banitto) are minor enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 12 in Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg, directly north of the landmark of Jabos Rock Rest Area. They can drop the Bunnit Sapling needed for Material Quest 3.

Smoke Cylinders (Japanese: , Shien no Entō) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in the Central Factory and Colony 6. According to their description, Dunban named them dubiously and they are pretty smoke-emitting cylinders.
Sky Shoes are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Ingredients For A Brew. They are commonly worn by High Entia.

Sleek Sandals are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are the strongest swimsuit type feet armor. They can be traded for with Zilex. It is part of the Sleek set of armour along with the Sleek Glasses, Sleek Oil, Sleek Cream and Sleek Trunks.
Sky Caps (Japanese: , Sukai Kyappu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Sleek Glasses (Japanese: , Mirukī Gurasu) are light head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are part of the swimsuit-style Sleek Set, along with Sleek Oil, Sleek Cream, Sleek Trunks, and Sleek Sandals. They can be acquired by trading on the Fallen Arm or by defeating several Mechon in Mechonis Field, the Central Factory, and Agniratha.
Sky Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are commonly worn by the High Entia.

Sleek Trunks are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They have the best defensive stats of all the swimsuit-style legs armour. They can be dropped by various Mechon on Mechonis, or traded for with Theo. They are part of the Sleek set of armour along with the Sleek Glasses, Sleek Oil, Sleek Cream and Sleek Sandals.
Sky Gloves are light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained as a quest reward after completing Sweet Seduction. They are commonly worn by High Entia.

Snow Cream is light arms armour in . It is made from fire-snow, which releases heat with it comes into contact with snow. It is part of the Snow set of armour along with the Snow Glasses, Snow Oil, Snow Trunks and Snow Sandals.
Sky Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be bought at the shop at Melfica Road Shop in Alcamoth.

Snow Oil is light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be dropped by various enemies, or be traded for with Kurralth. They are part of the Snow set of armour along with the Snow Glasses, Snow Cream, Snow Trunks and Snow Sandals.

Sleek Oil is light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It has the highest stats of all the swimsuit torso armour in the game, and can be traded for with Qofaria. It contains Mechon lubricant. It is part of the Sleek set of Armour along with the Sleek Glasses, Sleek Cream, Sleek Trunks and Sleek Sandals.

Sniper Paramecia (Japanese: , Sogeki no Paramishia) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 15 in the southwestern part of the Gaur Plain on Bionis' Leg, south of the Jabos Rock Rest Area. It can drop a Tirkin Tail Feather, which is needed for Material Quest 2.

The Sky Frying Pan is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be found at the northernmost point of the eastern part above the Sky Stage on the Bionis' Leg. The party is asked to collect it by Talonyth for Cook-Off Final Blow?!.
Snaer Strikers (Japanese: , Yukigakure no Tachi) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are swords wielded by Dunban, and can be acquired from a variety of sources.
Silence (Japanese: , Sairento, Silent) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are rifles that can be wielded by Sharla.
Silver Vasanovas (Japanese: , Ōgon no Vasanoba) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki.
The Siege Gnasher (Japanese: , Rōjō no Tsukutsuku) is a weapon in . It is a biter wielded by Riki.

Sleek Cream is light arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are the strongest swimsuit type gloves. An unslotted pair can be obtained by trading with Karlos. It is part of the Sleek set of Armour along with the Sleek Glasses, Sleek Oil, Sleek Trunks and Sleek Sandals.
The Silent Obelisk (Japanese: , Chinmoku no Oberisuku) is a landmark in . It is located in Satorl Marsh, west of the Glowing Obelisk.
Small Claws are common materials in . They can be dropped by Vangs in Tephra Cave, or be traded for in Colony 9.

The Smelly Perfume is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Obtaining it is one of two possible routes to complete Looking for Freedom, the other of which involves obtaining Pure Perfume. It can be found in the exact center of the Poison Swamp in Satorl Marsh.
Silver Rhogul Wings are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from various Rhoguls.
Slow Resist (Japanese: , Surou Teikō) is a Gem in that increases the chance of resisting Slow. __TOC__
Sleep Resist (Japanese: , Surīpu Teikō) is a Gem in Xenoblade Chronicles that increases the chance of resisting Sleep. __TOC__
Slow (Japanese: , Surou) is a Gem in that grants a chance that auto-attacks will inflict Slow on an enemy. __TOC__

Sloth Gogols are enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family, and can be found at level 74-76 northeast of Viliera Hill and north of Raguel Lake, among the cliffs on Bionis' Leg. Defeating eight of them is required to complete the quest Homs Determination given by Perrine in Colony 6. They can drop the Gogol Horns needed for A Token of Friendship and Colony 6 Reconstruction.
Sneaky (Japanese: , Moratta mo) is one of Riki's physical arts in . The art's damage is tripled if used from the enemy's rear.

Singing Brogs (Japanese: , Shingu Guroggu) are enemies in . They are members of the Brog family, and can be found at level 8 in Tephra Cave South of Mag Mell Ruins. Two of them must be defeated to complete Colony 9's Monster Quest 4 - Part 2. They are the only enemies that drop Croaking Brog Bags, two of which are needed to complete the quest The Plan - Preparation.

Shutdown (Japanese: , Shattodaun) is one of Fiora's physical arts in . It may inflict Sleep on an enemy. Buffs and debuffs will also be cleared from Mechon. Shutdown causes a large knockback effect, making it useful for moving an enemy into a hazard.

Sky Rhoguls (Japanese: , Sukai Rōguru) are enemies in . They are members of the Rhogul family, and can be found at level 18 on the Splintered Path in Colony 6 before the events at Mechonis Core. They are Sight monsters.

Sniper Tirkins (Japanese: , Sunaipu Tākin) are enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found from level 15-18 in Gaur Plain and the Tirkin Headquarters on Bionis' Leg. They can drop the Tirkin Tail Feathers needed for Material Quest 2.

Sinful Lamorak (Japanese: , Genzai no Ramorakku) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Mechon, and can be found at level 63 in the Central Factory. It appears suddenly when the party enters the room immediately southwest of the Tower Boarding Gate. It can drop the Reinforced Plungers needed for Best Boots.

The Silver Ring is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. Finding it is the objective of Search Quest 2 in Alcamoth. It can be found in the Imperial Palace, in a hallway in the southern end of the Great Hall.
Smelly Hides are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Leg Armus, Leg Arduns, or Daughter Armus.
Smelly Antennae are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Satorl Caterpiles and Bunker Wisps, or be traded for with Zazadan.

Small Upa Lights are rare materials in . They can be dropped by various Upas in the Ether Mine or Colony 6 or be traded for with Dulland, Zel Argentis, and Mefimefi in Colony 6. According to their description, they are too small to light up the darkness, but their glow does light up the heart.
Small Oars are common materials in . They can be dropped by Upas or Lizards around Colony 6, or be traded for.

Skill Points, commonly referred to as SP, are game mechanics in . They are similar to EXP and AP. SP are used to upgrade the party members' Skill Trees, and can be earned by battling and discovering Landmarks. __NOTOC__

Simius (Japanese: , Shimiusu; English dub: ) are large, four-armed simian creatures found on Mira in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The term simius is both singular and plural. Simius bear a loose resemblance to Cantors and a strong resemblance to Gogols, although the latter are not present in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

Sniper Rifles are ranged weapons in . They are the ranged weapons used by the Partisan Eagle and Astral Crusader Classes. No playable characters, other than Cross, outside these classes can wield them. Sniper Rifles are also the ranged weapons used by Lao, Bozé, and Al.
Smooth Recovery is one of Irina's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn this Art after completing the mission Renewed Will.
Sky High is one of Phog's two Signature Arts in . Cross learns this art after completing A Great Divide.
Slayonet is one of Bozé's two Signature Arts in . It is a Sniper Rifle Art. Cross can learn this art after completing the Affinity Mission Bozé's Ignorance.
Sickle Rock Rise (Japanese: , Shīkuru-gan no Oka) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, northwest of East Gate Plain.

Silver Suids (Japanese: , Shirubā Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 41-43 near FN Site 108 in Primordia during the day. Two of them must be defeated during Elma's Task A. They can drop the Suid Fillet needed for Suid Sirloin.

Silver Femina Suids (Japanese: , Shirubā Femina Zūsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Suid family, and can be found at level 41-43 near FN Site 108 in Primordia. Two of them must be defeated during Elma's Task B.

The Skybound Coil Tree (Japanese: , Shikū Daimakigi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a large tree located in Noctilum, on the Decapotamon south of FN Site 218. The upper branches connect to the Nopon Braidbridge. Mia can be found on the upper boughs after Mamma Mia! has been completed.

Skills are a battle mechanic in . They are unlocked by reaching certain Class Ranks in certain Classes, and can be leveled up by spending Battle Points. During battles several buff and debuff effects occur depending on the selected Skills. There are 94 in total. Some Classes have different amounts of skill slots available to assign a skill. Drifter has 5 skill slots. Generally, level 2 classes have 2 skill slots, level 3 classes have 3 skill slots, and level 4 classes have 4 skill slots. The exceptions to this rule are Striker, Samurai Gunner, and Duelist, which all have 1 less skill slot than standard for their level. Different skills are obtained by increasing a character's class rank, wit
Silhouette Tectinsulas (Japanese: , Shiruetto Tapenta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Tectinsula family, and can be found at level 36-38 near FN Site 205 in Noctilum.
Silent Murras (Japanese: , Sairento Tondomu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Murra family, and can be found at level 21-22 at White Phosphor Lake in Cauldros.

Sirene, the Lost (Japanese: , Maigo no Shirēnu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Lepyx family. It can be found at level 13 at FN Site 114 in Primordia, near East Gate Plain and Roof Rock. It must be defeated during the eponymous Basic Mission Sirene, the Lost.

Sludge Caecuses (Japanese: , Surajji Doren) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Caecus family, and can be found at level 26-29 in Noctilum on the beaches of Coil Tree Cape. They can drop Slimy Epitheliums, five of which are needed for Booming Business.
The Skell License is an Important Item in . It is obtained by completing The Skell License. It allows the player to purchase Skells at the Shop Terminal in Armory Alley.

The Slab Cinucula (Japanese: , Burokku Vasaruto) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Cinicula family. It is fought at level 24 in the Arendt Bridge in Primordia during Close Encounters.

Si-el, the Vacuous (Japanese: , Shinkū no Shi-eru) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is an Oc-serv machine. It can be found at level 19 at Qing Long Glade in Noctilum, hidden south of the Qing Long Glade BC. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Si-el, the Vacuous.

Skygazer's Atrium (Japanese: , Hoshimimado) is a Scenic Viewpoint in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a ledge in Noctilum above the Weeping Whitewood, and can be reached by taking the path toward the Weeping Whitewood from the Ensconced Citadel. As with all Scenic Viewpoints, its discovery yields an achievement ("The View from Skygazer's Atrium"). There are no enemies here, but several Pike Insidia reside on the path from the Citadel.

Slasher Beetles (Japanese: , Zangekiookabuto) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular around FN Site 313 and FN Site 317, or near the Drowning Ring.

Silvery Cactaceous Resins (Japanese: , Kwogoru no Hakugin Nendo) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in particular along the river from King's Falls to Balance Rock. It appears with greater frequency in early morning and in rain. Two of them are required for the mission Mayday.
Sleeping Amaryllises (Japanese: , Neruamaririsu) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Silver Papils (Japanese: , Shirubā Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 32-35 at Beehive Rock in Oblivia at daytime.

Sneaking Blattas (Japanese: , Sunīku Buratta) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 11-20 at Wonderment Bluff in Primordia during daytime.

Silvestre, the Morning Light (Japanese: , Gyōkō no Shiruvesutoru) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Levitath family. It can be found at level 48 at Drowning Ring in Oblivia. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Silvestre, the Morning Light.
Simius Snack Stashes are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Simius.
Sluggish Saltats (Japanese: , Suraggu Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 51-53 on Oblivia's Floating Reef.

Smalt Arenatects (Japanese: , Sumaruto Rorongu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Arenatect family, and can be found at level 21-30 in Sylvalum, in the western portions of Needle Rock Sandsea and South Ciel Sandsea.
Skulker Germivores (Japanese: , Rāku Burōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Germivore family, and can be found at level 9-10 near Seabird's Beak BC in Sylvalum.
Silver Vita Cores are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained with Reward Tickets, from the Vita, and possibly from other Vita Mechanoids.

Sky Aetrygons (Japanese: , Sukai Derupinu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Aetrygon family, and can be found at level 34-35 above Needle Rock Sandsea and at level 36-37 near Xanadu Overlook in Sylvalum.
Sizzling Visigels (Japanese: , Hotto Narukī) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Visigel family, and can be found at level 1-10 at FN Site 505 in Cauldros.

Slovity Pagus (Japanese: , Surabuti Peigasu) is a NPC in . She is a Cavern Clan Prone, leader of Team Slovity, and can be found at the East Gate in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles during Slovity's Rampage and on the Starboard side of the Ma-non Ship after that point.

Sniper Barrel is a Ranged Art in . It is a Multigun exclusive art, and it can be obtained after completing after completing Yelv's final affinity mission. It deals Ether damage and inflicts Stun on Shocked targets.
Smelly Fish Meats are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Purgovents or Lophids.
Skell Repair: Balancer is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a male mechanic and the primary destination is Primordia.

Skell License Certificates are Important Items in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are obtained by completing the eight Proficiency Exam missions, and all eight are required to complete The Skell License.
Silver Sacrifole Feathers are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Sacrifoles in Cauldros.
The Silver Xiphias Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Wilbur and is needed to complete Trade Agreement.
Sin'luarb is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is an Orphean who can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles at nighttime.

The Silver Mortifole Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained either from Pirapira by trading in 5 Coaletris, 2 Meteo Eaters and the Bronze Cinicula Card, or from Tika by trading in one Ashizel and the Silver Simius Card. It is needed to complete Trade Agreement.
Skell Crush is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It may trigger when a character's Skell loses an appendage.

Slovity's Rampage (Japanese: , Surabuti no Shin'i, Slovity's True Motive) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Trigo Bamboth near the East Gate in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles, after Cavern Crushers has been completed.
The Legen-dar is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is recovered from a Terebra near Biahno Lake in Primordia during one route of Setting Forth.
The Silver Simius Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Paqu Qadossi and is needed to complete Trade Agreement.

The Silver Evello Card is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is obtained from Lonlon by trading in one Red Simius Mane and the Silver Simius Card. It is needed to complete Trade Agreement.

Slovity's Revenge (Japanese: , Surabiti no Fukushū) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received by talking to Slovity Pagus on the Starboard side the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles.

Snipe Hunt (Japanese: , Zantō Sunaipā, The Remnant Sniper) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Bihabba on the Deck of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles. Route A requires searching NLA for a witness. The sniper is known to have fired from Talon Rock Summit, so the search can be limited to parts of NLA with a clear view of that location. The witnesses are a woman on a balcony in the southeast corner of Ishmael Hills, and a female BLADE in front of BLADE Tower. Finding either of them will satisfy the objective.
Skell Repair: Arm is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a Female Mechanic and the primary destination is Noctilum.

The Siphon Qmoeva (Japanese: , Dorō Kumūba) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 39 grey Qmoeva equipped with a Spike Cannon and two Boggle Bombs. It is found in Oblivia's Jair Fortress during A Dish Served Cold and must be defeated within ten minutes.
Simius Smackdown is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from Dorian Caravan to defeat Mortal Simius in Oblivia.
Skell Maintenance is a Basic Mission in . It is a request from Matthew and the primary destination is the Industrial District of New Los Angeles.
Skell Repair: Antenna is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a female mechanic and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Skell Repair: Cylinder is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a male mechanic to obtain New Cylinders and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Skell Repair: Frame is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a mechanic to obtain Genuine Frames.
Skell Repair: Head is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request to obtain a Galdr Head for a mechanic and the primary destination is Cauldros.
Skell Repair: Optics is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a male mechanic and the primary destination is Cauldros.
Skell Repair: Plunger is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a female mechanic and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Skell Repair: Thruster is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a male mechanic and the primary destination is Cauldros.
The Signature Glaive: Allegiance is a melee weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 60 Longsword dropped by the tyrant Shuravas, the Enraged from its back fin appendage.

Silver Blatta Wings are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from white Blattas, or for 24 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in Arts: Recover HP I and V augments.

Silver Petramand Silk are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Petramands with green acid sacs, or for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX TP Rebound and Damage.GP-GAIN augments.

Silver Progen Wings are rare materials in . They can be obtained from brown Progen, for 72 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks, or for 30 Material Tickets from the Material Market in . They are components in Extend Overdrive I and V augments.
Silver Yggralith Nuts are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Yggralith Zero.
Simius A is a Holofigure in . It depicts a red-haired simius variant. It can be obtained from Hayreddin, the Territorial in Primordia.
Simius B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a green-haired simius variant. It can be obtained from Demetrio, the Tempestuous in Noctilum.
Simius C is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a golden-haired simius variant. It can be obtained from Diogenes, the Covetous in Oblivia.
Snack Time is a special Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Nopon about to be eaten by a Prone. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Normal Mission Slovity's Rampage.

Slair Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Longsword. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Fruits category of the Sylvalum Collectopedia. The Slair weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Slair * Iron Slair * Carbide Slair * Cermet Slair * Chrome Slair * Chromoly Slair * Cobalt Slair * Titanium Slair * Ceramic Slair * Diamond Slair * Ultra Diamond Slair

Slair II Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Longsword. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Insects category of the Noctilum Collectopedia. The Slair II weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Slair II * Iron Slair II * Carbide Slair II * Cermet Slair II * Chrome Slair II * Chromoly Slair II * Cobalt Slair II * Titanium Slair II * Ceramic Slair II * Diamond Slair II

Smoke 'Em Out is a Squad Mission in . It is part of BLADE Mission No.14, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting six Diluses. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.
Side Attack Plus is a ground weapon attack Augment in and that increases damage dealt when attacking from the side of an enemy. The Skell equivalent is PositionDmg.SIDE.
Slayer.THEROID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Theroids dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Theroid Slayer.

Slow Arts is a stat debuff in Xenoblade Chronicles X. Slow Arts increases Cooldown time for party members' Battle Arts and the time between their Auto-Attacks, and reduces the rate at which enemies use Battle Arts.
The Signature Glaive: Four Virtues is a unique melee weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 40 Longsword dropped by the tyrant Chantai, the Insect Maiden.

Slayer.ULTRAFAUNA is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Ultrafauna dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Ultrafauna Slayer.

Slayer.INSECTOID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Insectoids dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Insectoid Slayer.

Slayer.PISCINOID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage dealt by the Skell against Piscinoids by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Piscinoid Slayer.

Slayer.HUMANOID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Humanoids dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Humanoid Slayer.

Slayer.MECHANOID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Mechanoids dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Mechanoid Slayer.

Slayer.CHIMEROID is an enemy exploit Skell weapon augment in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It boosts the damage against Chimeroids dealt by the Skell by 2% to 40%. It is the Skell equivalent of Chimeroid Slayer.
The Signature Glaive: Fledgling is a one-of-a-kind melee weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is Nagi's Longsword, part of his initial gear when he is recruited, and cannot be obtained elsewhere.

Sky Jewels are rare materials in . It can be obtained from the Radiant Pterix in Satorl Marsh. Sky Jewels are also available for trade via overtrade with En Argentis if she has moved to Colony 6 over Zel Argentis and Perrine in Colony 9 if she has not moved or if Mefimefi has moved over her. According to their description, they are gemstones containing the sky, which unfolds expansively inside them.
Slender Horns are common materials in . They can be dropped by Hoxes in Colony 6, or traded for.
Slimy Epitheliums are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by various Ekidnos, Chloro Laias, or they can be obtained by trading.
Slit Edge (Japanese: , Suritto Ejji) is one of Shulk's physical arts in and . When used from the side it inflicts Phys Def Down, reducing the enemy's Physical Defence by 50%.
Small Dorsal Fins are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Leg Piranhax and Mellow Sardi, and can also be traded for.
Small Insect Legs are materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are common materials, and can be dropped by many Insect Enemies. They cannot be traded for.

Small Scales are common materials in . They can only be dropped by Colony Piranhax in Colony 9, and traded for with Cheryl, Narine, and Kantz. According to their description, they are popularly worn by kids as a badge and prettier ones are a sign of affluence. One is needed for Colony 9's Material Quest 2.

Small Shells (Japanese: , Chiisana kōra) are common materials in . They can be dropped by various Krabbles in Colony 9, or traded for with Betty, Dorothy, and Raoul. According to their description, turning them upside down makes them usable as pots to cook for three to four people. Two are needed for Colony 9's Material Quest 1.
The Slice of Bread is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is recieved from Moimoi, who asks that it be delivered to his brother Muimui during Bread and a Circus.

Shynini's Accessories (Japanese: , Akusesarī Kirakira) is a shop in . It is run by Shynini and can be found at Argentum Bazaar in the Argentum Trade Guild's Goldmouth. Accessories for Drivers can be purchased here.

Siren (Japanese: , Seirēn) is an Artifice in . It is a large machine that resides high above Alrest, and is able to shoot its particle cannon down wherever Mythra directs it. After finishing the game, installing Patch (Ver.1.3.0), and starting a New Game Plus, Siren will take part in a Level IV Blade Special for Pneuma. It will fire a gigantic beam towards Pneuma's desired location, inflicting large amounts of damage.

Smash is a status in and . It causes a Launched target to be smacked down to the ground, inflicting massive damage. Smash is instantaneous. Arts that inflict Smash are designated by a large white downwards arrow. When an enemy is Smashed, its Launch condition is immediately ended and can therefore act, but it does take a moment to pick itself up.
